chunks: From him, from Ibn Abī Naṣr, from ʿĪsā ibn Mihrān, from Abī Ghānim, from Minhāl ibn Khalīl, from Salamah ibn Tamām, who said:

A man poured a pot containing broth over another man's head, and his hair fell out. They brought their dispute over that to ʿAlī عليه السلام, so he gave him respite for one year. Then he came back and his hair had not grown again, so he ruled against him with the diyah.

key_terms.أَجَّلَهُ: he granted a delay or set a waiting period
key_terms.بِٱلدِّيَةِ: with the diyah, meaning financial compensation for bodily injury
key_terms.سَنَةً: one year, used to determine whether the hair loss was permanent
key_terms.شَعْرُهُ: his hair, which was lost because of the injury
key_terms.مَرَقٌ: broth or soup contained in the pot
key_terms.ٱخْتَصَمُوا: they disputed or brought a legal complaint

ai.seo_question: What did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام rule when a person's hair was permanently lost due to injury?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a judicial ruling by Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام concerning bodily injury. When a man's hair did not grow back after a year following harm done to him, Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام ruled that full compensation was due, showing measured adjudication based on the lasting effect of the injury.
